arxiv-2111-06428.title: A deterministic algorithm for Harder-Narasimhan filtrations for representations of acyclic quivers
arxiv-2111-06428.creator: chi-yu Cheng
arxiv-2111-06428.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by chi-yu Cheng. Let M M be a representation of an acyclic quiver Q Q over an infinite field k k . We establish a deterministic algorithm for computing the Harder-Narasimhan filtration of M M . The algorithm is polynomial in the dimensions of M M , the weights that induce the Harder-Narasimhan filtration of M M , and the number of paths in Q Q .

arxiv-2201-11730.title: The Page Curve for Reflected Entropy
arxiv-2201-11730.creator: Chris Akers, Thomas Faulkner, Simon Lin, and Pratik Rath
arxiv-2201-11730.description: Abstract We study the reflected entropy S R S_{R} in the West Coast Model, a toy model of black hole evaporation consisting of JT gravity coupled to end-of-the-world branes. We demonstrate the validity of the holographic duality relating it to the entanglement wedge cross section away from phase transitions.

arxiv-2305-02960.title: Majorizing Measures, Codes, and Information
arxiv-2305-02960.creator: Yifeng Chu, Maxim Raginsky
arxiv-2305-02960.description: Abstract The majorizing measure theorem of Fernique and Talagrand is a fundamental result in the theory of random processes. It relates the boundedness of random processes indexed by elements of a metric space to complexity measures arising from certain multiscale combinatorial structures, such as packing and covering trees.

arxiv-2309-03718.title: Compactness of conformal Chern-minimal surfaces in Hermitian surface
arxiv-2309-03718.creator: Xiaowei Xu
arxiv-2309-03718.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Xiaowei Xu. The Chern-minimal surfaces in Hermitian surface play a similar role as minimal surfaces in Kähler surface (see [ 11 ] ) from the viewpoint of submanifolds. This paper studies the compactness of Chern-minimal surfaces.

arxiv-2409-14252.title: Collaborative Text Editing with Eg-walker: Better, Faster, Smaller
arxiv-2409-14252.creator: Joseph Gentle, Martin Kleppmann
arxiv-2409-14252.description: Abstract . Collaborative text editing algorithms allow several users to concurrently modify a text file, and automatically merge concurrent edits into a consistent state. Existing algorithms fall in two categories: Operational Transformation (OT) algorithms are slow to merge files that have diverged substantially due to offline editing; CRDTs are slow to load and consume a lot of memory.

arxiv-2410-22839.title: Danoliteracy of Generative Large Language Models
arxiv-2410-22839.creator: Søren Vejlgaard Holm, Lars Kai Hansen, Martin Carsten Nielsen
arxiv-2410-22839.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Søren Vejlgaard Holm, Lars Kai Hansen, Martin Carsten Nielsen. The language technology moonshot moment of Generative Large Language Models (GLLMs) was not limited to English: These models brought a surge of technological applications, investments, and hype to low-resource languages as well. However, the capabilities of these models in languages such as Danish were, until recently, difficult to verify beyond qualitative demonstrations due to a lack of applicable evaluation corpora.

arxiv-2412-16438.title: Modelling visibility and surface deformation in particle-fluid flow fields generated by helicopter rotors
arxiv-2412-16438.creator: S. Langdon, D. J. Needham
arxiv-2412-16438.description: Abstract As a helicopter descends towards a bed of sand, a high velocity particle laden cloud can form around the helicopter body, a phenomenon known as “brownout”, and a consequence of which can potentially be a significant deterioration in visibility for the helicopter pilot.

arxiv-2502-04923.title: Cached Multi-Lora Composition for Multi-Concept Image Generation
arxiv-2502-04923.creator: Xiandong Zou, Mingzhu Shen, Christos-Savvas Bouganis, Yiren Zhao
arxiv-2502-04923.description: Abstract Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) has emerged as a widely adopted technique in text-to-image models, enabling precise rendering of multiple distinct elements, such as characters and styles, in multi-concept image generation. However, current approaches face significant challenges when composing these LoRAs for multi-concept image generation, particularly as the number of LoRAs increases, resulting in diminished generated image quality.

arxiv-2502-16124.title: ZIA: A Theoretical Framework for Zero-Input AI
arxiv-2502-16124.creator: Aditi De
arxiv-2502-16124.description: Abstract Zero-Input AI (ZIA) introduces a novel framework for human-computer interaction by enabling proactive intent prediction without explicit user commands. It integrates gaze tracking, bio-signals (EEG, heart rate), and contextual data (time, location, usage history) into a multi-modal model for real-time inference, targeting <100 ms latency.

arxiv-2509-04564.title: The Evolution and Internal Structure of Neptunes and Sub-Neptunes
arxiv-2509-04564.creator: Mark Eberlein, Ravit Helled
arxiv-2509-04564.description: Abstract Context. Neptunes and sub-Neptunes are typically modeled under the assumption that the interior is adiabatic and consists of distinct layers. However, this assumption is oversimplified as formation models indicate that composition gradients can exist. Such composition gradients can significantly affect the planetary thermal evolution by inhibiting convection.

arxiv-2509-21330.title: Interpretable Spectral Features Predict Conductivity in Self-Driving Doped Conjugated Polymer Labs
arxiv-2509-21330.creator: Ankush Kumar Mishra, Jacob P. Mauthe, Nicholas Luke, Aram Amassian, Baskar Ganapathysubramanian
arxiv-2509-21330.description: Abstract Self-driving labs (SDLs) promise faster materials discovery by coupling automation with machine learning, but a central challenge is predicting costly, slow-to-measure properties from inexpensive, automatable readouts. We address this for doped conjugated polymers by learning interpretable spectral fingerprints from optical spectroscopy to predict electrical conductivity.

arxiv-2510-20344.title: Neural Networks for Censored Expectile Regression Based on Data Augmentation
arxiv-2510-20344.creator: Wei Cao, Shanshan Wang
arxiv-2510-20344.description: Abstract Expectile regression neural networks (ERNNs) are powerful tools for capturing heterogeneity and complex nonlinear structures in data. However, most existing research has primarily focused on fully observed data, with limited attention paid to scenarios involving censored observations. In this paper, we propose a data augmentation–based ERNNs algorithm, termed DAERNN , for modeling heterogeneous censored data.

arxiv-2601-02011.title: Cyclists’ Cardiac Conundrum
arxiv-2601-02011.creator: Andrew Nugent, Yi Ting Loo, Jack Buckingham
arxiv-2601-02011.description: Abstract Arrhythmia is an abnormality of the heart’s rhythm, caused by problems in the conductive system and resulting in irregular heartbeats. There is increasing evidence that undertaking frequent endurance sports training elevates one’s risk of arrhythmia. Arrhythmia is diagnosed using an electrocardiogram (ECG) but this is not typically available to athletes while exercising.

arxiv-2601-11064.title: Spectral Signatures of Heavy Quarkonia in a Rotating and Anisotropic Quark-Gluon Plasma: A Holographic Study
arxiv-2601-11064.creator: Xiang-Wei Shi, Sheng-Qin Feng
arxiv-2601-11064.description: Abstract We investigate the in-medium spectral functions and effective masses of heavy quarkonia charmonium ( J / Ψ J/\Psi ) and bottomonium ( Υ ⁡ ( 1 ​ S ) \Upsilon(1S) ) in a quark-gluon plasma (QGP) possessing both global rotation and spatial anisotropy.

pmc-10502983.title: Rhythm of relationships in a social fish over the course of a full year in the wild
pmc-10502983.creator: Christopher T Monk, Ulf Aslak, Dirk Brockmann, Robert Arlinghaus
pmc-10502983.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundAnimals are expected to adjust their social behaviour to cope with challenges in their environment. Therefore, for fish populations in temperate regions with seasonal and daily environmental oscillations, characteristic rhythms of social relationships should be pronounced. To date, most research concerning fish social networks and biorhythms has occurred in artificial laboratory environments or over confined temporal scales of days to weeks.

pmc-10565315.title: Evaluating a social and emotional well-being model of service piloted in Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Services in Western Australia: an Aboriginal Participatory Action Research approach
pmc-10565315.creator: Patricia Dudgeon, Emma Carlin, Kate Derry, Joanna Alexi, Michael Mitchell, Rama Putu Agung-Igusti
pmc-10565315.description: IntroductionThe delivery of services to improve Aboriginal health and well-being must centre culture and integrate a social and emotional well-being understanding and approaches. These approaches are essential in increasing access to, and engagement with, health services, as well as ensuring culturally safe, person-centred and community-centred care.

pmc-11516613.title: Document Indigenous Food Ingredients in China through Youth Participation
pmc-11516613.creator: Z Wang, M Ma, Y Li
pmc-11516613.description: ProblemIndigenous food systems can affect multiple aspects of Indigenous people’s health and contribute to more efficient, sustainable, resilient, and equitable food systems. However, although tens of Indigenous groups live in China, very few projects have targeted their traditional or Indigenous food systems and ingredients.

pmc-11531584.title: Virtual screening, ADMET prediction, molecular docking, and dynamic simulation studies of natural products as BACE1 inhibitors for the management of Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-11531584.creator: Davood Gheidari, Morteza Mehrdad, Zahra karimelahi
pmc-11531584.description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a degenerative neurological disorder that chronically and irreversibly affects memory, cognitive function, learning ability, and organizational skills. Numerous studies have demonstrated BACE1 as a critical therapeutic target for AD, emphasizing the need for specific inhibition of BACE1 to develop effective therapeutics. However, current BACE1 inhibitors have certain limitations.

pmc-11568779.title: Metabolic engineering of Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1 for naringenin production
pmc-11568779.creator: Kesi Kurnia, Elena Efimova, Ville Santala, Suvi Santala
pmc-11568779.description: Naringenin, a flavanone and a precursor for a variety of flavonoids, has potential applications in the health and pharmaceutical sectors. The biological production of naringenin using genetically engineered microbes is considered as a promising strategy. The naringenin synthesis pathway involving chalcone synthase (CHS) and chalcone isomerase (CHI) relies on the efficient supply of key substrates, malonyl-CoA and p-coumaroyl-CoA.

pmc-11712152.creator: Aygun Badalova
pmc-11712152.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundProper name anomia is a common experience that can become amplified in patients with a diagnosis of dementia (PWD). app aims to provide practice‐based therapy for PWD to relearn the names of key people in their lives. It has been developed using the principles of errorless learning and spaced retrieval, which have previously been shown to improve the remembering the familiar people’s names and benefit the relationship between the PWD and their loved ones. pmc-12607961.title: Expanding Cancer Prevention: Strategies Integrated into Occupational Health Surveillance
pmc-12607961.creator: Giulia Collatuzzo, Alessandro Godono, Giulia Fiorini, Daniel Vencovsky, Stefano Giordani, Valentina Biagioli, Felipe Augusto Pinto-Vidal, Monireh Sadat Seyyedsalehi, Magdalena Kostrzewa, Angel Honrado, Daniele Bruno, Adonina Tardon, Dana Mates, Anna Schneider-Kamp, Eleonora Fabianova, Paolo Boffetta
pmc-12607961.description: Simple SummaryIn a landscape where population aging and scarce control of modifiable risk factors contribute to unfavorable cancer patterns, strategies aimed at raising awareness and increasing participation in cancer screening are urgent. Several barriers related to both individual and environmental factors impair the participation in available cancer prevention screening. This critical issue particularly concerns disadvantaged subgroups.

pmc-12664720.title: Comprehensive Bioinformatics Analysis and Validation of the Mechanism of Glutamic-pyruvic Transaminase 2 in Bladder Cancer
pmc-12664720.creator: Haonan Dong, Hongqiong Li, Shi Chen, Qun Wang, Yawei Zhang, Hongjin Shi, Jieming Zuo, Junhao Chen, Jiansong Wang, Haifeng Wang
pmc-12664720.description: Objective: Glutamic pyruvic transaminase 2 (GPT2) promotes the initiation and progression of various cancers. However, its regulatory role in bladder cancer (BCa) remains unclear. In this study, we aimed to validate the role of GPT2 in BCa using bioinformatics analysis combined with in vitro and in vivo experiments.

pmc-12703687.title: Efficacy and safety of twice-daily accelerated hyperfractionated re-irradiation for thoracic malignancies☆
pmc-12703687.creator: Victoria L. Doss, Cecilia F.P.M. de Sousa, Elaina Hales, Tinker Trent, Esi Hagan, Tsion Gebre, Anas Obaideen, Meti Negassa, Dezhi Liu, Chen Hu, Akila N. Viswanathan, Heng Li, K.Ranh Voong, Xun Jia, Todd McNutt, Rachel B. Ger, Russell K. Hales
pmc-12703687.description: Introduction:Balancing the demands for dose-escalated re-irradiation with toxicity to organs at risk (OARs) is a challenge. Twice-daily (BID) accelerated hyperfractionated re-irradiation (re-RT) is a potential solution, yet there is no guidance for its application for thoracic malignancies.Methods:All BID thoracic re-RT cases at our institution since 2014 were reviewed. Prior radiation courses were deformably registered.

pmc-13153357.title: The ventilatory response to arousal from sleep is elevated in young individuals with post-traumatic stress disorder symptoms
pmc-13153357.creator: Maya T Schenker, Amber Russell, Darsh Cherian, Yuhe Pan, Gemma Bruce, Lilith Zeng, Joanne Avraam, Fergal J O’Donoghue, Kim L Felmingham, Amy S Jordan
pmc-13153357.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeObstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is reported to be more prevalent in posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) compared to the general population for unknown reasons. Most prior studies have assessed military populations who commonly possess other OSA risk factors.

pmc-13342898.title: Metabolic and bone effects of long-acting polyethylene glycol-recombinant human growth hormone in growth hormone deficiency during the transition period: a prospective study
pmc-13342898.creator: Ke Huang, Hu Lin, Lifen Chen, Zhiya Dong, Yanhong Li, Guimei Li, Hui Yao, Shouyue Sun, Junfen Fu
pmc-13342898.description: Purpose Polyethylene glycol-recombinant human growth hormone (PEG-rhGH) is the first commercial long-acting rhGH preparation approved in China. This study was designed to assess the efficacy and safety of PEG-rhGH in treating growth hormone deficiency (GHD) during the transition period.Methods A prospective, multicenter and single-arm study was performed.

pmc-13586870.description: SummaryElectric arc furnace (EAF) steelmaking underpins China’s low-carbon steel transition, while uneven regional resources and energy conditions greatly constrain its low-carbon development. This study adopts a province-level material flow analysis-capacity integration framework with multi-scenario modeling to explore targeted regional decarbonization pathways. Although national scrap supply generally meets domestic EAF demand, severe provincial mismatches occur: major producers, including Hebei (36.

pmc-13633516.title: Single-stage microscopic and endoscopic resection of spatially separate meningiomas through a single craniotomy
pmc-13633516.creator: Takuya Kitamura, Kento Takahara, Hirotsugu Nogawa, Nobuhiro Yamada, Masahiro Ogino
pmc-13633516.description: Background: Multiple meningiomas are frequently encountered; however, determining the optimal surgical strategy for single-stage resection can be challenging. Conventional approaches include performing multiple craniotomies or a single large craniotomy encompassing both lesions, which may be overly invasive depending on patient factors and tumor characteristics.
